sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or identify).

questions.q: State the full form: (a) NABARD (b) SIDBI.
questions.answer:
(a) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
(b) Small Industries Development Bank of India

questions.q: Identify the type of bank: (a) a commercial bank in which the majority of share capital is held by private individuals; (b) the bank that assists and guides the export of products.
questions.answer:
(a) Private sector bank
(b) EXIM Bank (Export-Import Bank of India)

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The counterfoil of the pay-in-slip is returned to the ________ by the bank. (b) The right-hand part of the pay-in-slip is called the ________.
questions.answer:
(a) depositor (account holder)
(b) foil

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Deposits in a savings bank account serve present as well as future needs. (b) A fixed amount must be deposited every month in a Fixed Deposit Account.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — that is a recurring deposit; an FD is a single lump sum for a fixed period.

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) A savings account holder cannot introduce another person when opening a savings account. (b) The passbook must be presented to the bank for entering deposits and withdrawals.
questions.answer:
(a) False — an existing account holder can introduce a new customer.
(b) True

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) A cheque is attached to the ________ before depositing. (b) Before paying a cheque, the signature is verified with the ________.
questions.answer:
(a) pay-in-slip
(b) specimen signature (card) kept by the bank

questions.q: State the full form: (a) CBS (b) UPI.
questions.answer:
(a) Core Banking Solution
(b) Unified Payments Interface

questions.q: Give one-word answers: (a) Can an illiterate person be issued a debit card? (b) Name the system used for both fund transfers and bill payments.
questions.answer:
(a) Yes
(b) UPI (Unified Payments Interface)

questions.q: A digital payment system lets a user transact with Aadhaar number and fingerprint or iris; the account must be linked to Aadhaar. (a) Name the system. (b) Why is it considered safe?
questions.answer:
(a) AEPS — Aadhaar Enabled Payment System.
(b) It uses biometric authentication, which cannot easily be copied.

questions.q: State the full form: (a) KYC (b) ATM.
questions.answer:
(a) Know Your Customer
(b) Automated Teller Machine

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) The rate at which money is lent or borrowed is the interest rate. (b) When a banker accepts securities for safe custody, the relation between banker and customer is that of principal and agent.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — it is bailor (customer) and bailee (banker).

questions.q: Write True (T) or False (F): (a) Overdraft can be given on a current account. (b) For a bank, deposits are an asset.
questions.answer:
(a) True
(b) False — deposits are a liability (money owed to depositors).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Mr. Ravi has a limited income and wants to save for future needs. Which account should he open? Why?
questions.answer: A savings bank account — it can be opened with a small amount, money can be deposited any time, it earns interest and can be withdrawn when needed.

questions.q: Mahesh's father wants to save ₹2,00,000 to gift Mahesh on his graduation day. Which deposit should he open?
questions.answer: A fixed deposit account — a lump sum is deposited for a fixed period and earns a higher rate of interest.

questions.q: State any two differences between a bank and a moneylender.
questions.answer:
(1) Regulation: a bank is regulated by the RBI; a moneylender is not.
(2) Interest: a bank's rate is governed by the RBI and reasonable; a moneylender's is decided by himself and usually very high.
(Also: banks accept deposits; recovery by banks is lawful and flexible.)

questions.q: Explain the working of net banking.
questions.answer: With net banking the customer logs on to the bank's website with a user ID and password and can, at any time, check the balance and statement, transfer funds, open a fixed deposit, and pay electricity, telephone and other bills without visiting the branch.

questions.q: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
questions.answer: A debit card pays from the holder's own bank balance, which is reduced at once. A credit card lets the holder buy on credit up to a limit and pay the bank later; interest is charged if not paid within the credit period.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is e-banking? Explain any two types of e-banking services.
questions.answer:
E-banking means doing banking transactions electronically through computers, mobile phones and cards without visiting the branch.
(1) ATM — withdraw cash, check balance, deposit money 24 hours a day.
(2) Net banking — transfer funds, pay bills and open deposits over the Internet.
(Also: debit and credit cards, mobile banking, UPI.)

questions.q: What is an ATM? How does it help bank customers?
questions.answer:
An Automated Teller Machine is an electronic machine installed by banks at convenient places.
It helps customers: (1) withdraw cash at any time, 24 × 7; (2) check balance and get a mini statement; (3) deposit cash and transfer funds without going to the branch.

or.q: State any three secondary functions of a commercial bank.
or.answer:
(1) Agency functions — collecting cheques, dividends and interest, paying premiums and bills for customers.
(2) Issuing demand drafts and traveller's cheques.
(3) Safe deposit lockers and safe custody of valuables; letters of credit; foreign exchange.

questions.q: Explain three modern trends of e-banking in India.
questions.answer:
(1) Net banking — banking over the Internet.
(2) Mobile banking and UPI — instant transfers and bill payments from the phone.
(3) ATMs, debit and credit cards — cash and cashless payments any time.

questions.q: Explain debit card and credit card.
questions.answer:
Debit card: issued to a savings or current account holder; payments made with it are deducted at once from his own balance.
Credit card: lets the holder buy goods on credit up to a fixed limit; the bank pays the seller and the holder repays within the credit period, after which interest is charged. It may be issued to persons with or without an account.

questions.q: Explain two types of cooperative banks. OR Explain the different modes of payment.
questions.answer:
Cooperative banks: (1) Primary credit societies — village-level societies giving small loans to members; (2) Central cooperative banks — district-level, finance the primary societies; (3) State cooperative banks — apex bank of the state.
Modes of payment: cash, cheque, demand draft, debit and credit cards, net banking and UPI transfers.

questions.q: Distinguish between a current deposit account and a savings bank account.
questions.answer:
Purpose: savings — for saving by individuals; current — for businesses to make and receive payments.
Withdrawals: savings — limited in number; current — any number.
Interest: savings — earns interest; current — little or none.
Overdraft: not on savings; allowed on current.

sections.title: Long answer questions, including case-based questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Banks provide funds for business and play a vital role in the development of a nation. Explain the role of banking.
questions.answer:
(1) Mobilising savings — banks collect the small savings of people and make them available for productive use.
(2) Finance for trade and industry — loans, cash credit and overdrafts help firms buy raw materials and machines.
(3) Help to agriculture and small industries through NABARD, SIDBI and priority-sector lending.
(4) Easy and safe payments — cheques, drafts, cards, net banking and UPI reduce the use of cash.
(5) Balanced regional development — branches in rural and backward areas, credit to weaker sections, promotion of exports.

questions.q: Commercial banks play a vital role in economic development through primary and secondary functions. Explain any five functions.
questions.answer:
(1) Accepting deposits — savings, current, fixed and recurring.
(2) Granting loans and advances — loans, cash credit, overdraft, discounting of bills.
(3) Agency functions — collecting cheques, dividends and interest; paying bills and premiums; buying and selling securities.
(4) General utility functions — demand drafts, traveller's cheques, lockers and safe custody.
(5) Letters of credit, foreign exchange and e-banking services.

questions.q: HDFC Bank offers many accounts. Geeta, a businesswoman, chose an account with the most liquid deposits and no limit on the number of transactions; her mother opened one for her savings with cheque facility; her brother Kartik deposits ₹3,000 every month for two years. (a) Identify the accounts. (b) Explain two other types of account.
questions.answer:
(a) Geeta — current deposit account; her mother — savings bank account; Kartik — recurring deposit account.
(b) Fixed deposit account — a lump sum kept for a fixed period at a higher interest rate.
Multiple option (flexi) deposit — a savings account where amounts above a limit move automatically to a fixed deposit and earn more interest.

or.q: Anil learns of an account at SBI in which amounts above a limit are transferred automatically to a fixed deposit, combining the benefits of savings and FD. Identify and explain it.
or.answer: Multiple option deposit account (flexi or sweep account). It works like a savings account for deposits and withdrawals, but when the balance exceeds a set limit the excess is automatically moved into a fixed deposit, earning the higher FD interest; when needed, money comes back from the FD to the savings account. So the customer gets both liquidity and higher interest.

questions.q: Describe the procedure of opening a savings bank account.
questions.answer:
(1) Find out the minimum initial deposit and ask for the account-opening form.
(2) Fill the form — name, address, occupation, nominee — and sign; attach photographs.
(3) Give KYC documents (proof of identity and address) and get the introduction of an existing account holder.
(4) Give the specimen signature.
(5) Deposit the initial amount with a pay-in-slip.
(6) The bank opens the account and issues a passbook, cheque book and ATM/debit card.
